## My thinking, in my own voice

Ay, 45 years I've been working this land. Me and my old man, just the two of us now on our 12 mu. The children all went to the city, they don't come back for planting anymore. So we do what we've always done — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same as my mother-in-law taught me.

**Wheat first.** I'll plant around early October, after the autumn rain if we get it. I use the seed I saved from last year's harvest, plus a little bought seed mixed in — my neighbor Old Wang's daughter-in-law got some new variety from the co-op, I watched her field, it did alright, so maybe I'll try a bag of that too. For base fertilizer I put down two bags of compound fert per mu before plowing — that's how I've always done it, the bag says 15-15-15 or something, I can't read it but the shop owner tells me. Then in spring when the wheat turns green again I topdress some urea, maybe one bag for every two mu. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing I'll put on a bit more, but urea is expensive this year, over 100 yuan a bag, so I try not to waste.

For water — the well is metered now, costs money every time I pump. I'll water once before winter (dongshui), once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain-filling if the sky is dry. Four times usually. If it rains I skip one. Pumping costs around 30 yuan a mu each time, adds up fast.

Plowing and sowing I hire the man with the tractor — 60 yuan a mu, he does the whole village. Harvest I hire the combine, another 60 yuan. My old man can't swing a sickle anymore, his back is bad. Pesticide I only spray if I see the aphids, usually one time in spring, cheap stuff.

**Then maize, right after wheat harvest in June.** Very tight, maybe five days to clear the straw and plant. I don't plow — just direct seed into the stubble with the hired planter, that's what everyone does now. Hybrid seed, I buy it every year, can't save hybrid seed, the shop has the same brand I've used four or five years running. One bag of compound fert at planting, maybe topdress urea once when the maize is knee-high if it rains and the leaves look pale. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat — I water once or twice if July is dry, sometimes not at all if the rain comes.

Herbicide after planting, one spray, keeps the weeds down so I don't have to hoe — my knees can't take hoeing anymore. Harvest in late September, hire the combine again.

**Money.** I count in my head — seeds, two bags fert per mu for wheat plus urea, maize seed and fert, hired machinery, water, one or two sprays. Maybe 600-700 yuan a mu for the whole year, both crops. Twelve mu so around 8,000 yuan in costs. If wheat gives me 400 kg a mu and maize 450 kg, and prices hold, we'll be alright. Not rich, but enough to eat and put a little aside. Same as last year. Same as every year.
